display.title: Episode 500: Little Avraham Searches for Hashem
display.summary_short: Why we hear the Torah read every three days, a six-year-old Shema guest, the story of little Avraham searching for the Creator, and a boy who learns the song 'Hashem Is Here'.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi explains why the Torah is read in shul on Monday, Thursday and Shabbos: after the Jews went three days in the desert without water, the Sages taught that we must never go three days without hearing the Torah, which is our living water. The Torah reader sings each word with the te'amim, the musical notes given at Har Sinai. In this week's sedra Avraham Avinu teaches the whole world about Hashem, and children can do the same by sharing their books and the Moshiach Times with a friend. After the Hakochainik march, a six-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time, 'living with the sedra': three-year-old Avraham walks by the sea wondering who made the world. He thinks it may be the sun, then the moon, then the stars, but each one disappears, until he understands that the Creator made them all, cannot be seen, and is everywhere. A second short story follows a little boy doing homework: how many directions can you point to? He counts six and teaches his mother the new song 'Hashem is here, Hashem is there, Hashem is truly everywhere', which closes the show.
display.lesson: Hashem, who created the sun, moon and stars, is everywhere at all times; like Avraham Avinu, we should tell others about Him.
